text_blocks.snippet: To tell if your roof has hail damage, you need to look for specific signs on the ground, on soft metal exterior items, and directly on the shingles.
snippet_highlighted_words: look for specific signs on the ground, on soft metal exterior items, and directly on the shingles

text_blocks.snippet: 1. Check the Ground and Exterior First
Before climbing onto the roof, look around your property for collateral signs of hail impact:

list.snippet: Granules in gutters: Check your downspouts, splash blocks, and driveways for piles of tiny, sand-like shingle granules washed off by rain.
Dented soft metals: Look at aluminum or steel gutters, downspouts, window screens, AC units, mailboxes, and roof/exhaust vents for fresh dings or dimples.
Other property damage: Check for dents on your car, cracked window screens, or bruised/shredded siding and painted wood.

text_blocks.snippet: If you are comfortable and safe getting onto the roof—or hire a professional—look closely at the asphalt shingles:

list.snippet: Dark bruised spots: Hail knocks off protective granules, leaving a dark, exposed spot of the underlying black asphalt mat.
Soft or spongy feel: Press gently on a suspected mark; a hail hit often breaks or fractures the fiberglass mat beneath, making the shingle feel soft or indented.

Chalk test trick: Rub a piece of sidewalk chalk sideways across the shingle; the chalk will pass over the intact surface but won't stick inside the sunken hail dimples, making the impact pattern stand out.

Random distribution: Hail hits appear randomly and scattered across a slope, unlike the even, uniform aging or blistering of normal weather wear. Insurance adjusters typically count hits inside a 10x10-foot test square (often looking for roughly 8 to 12 impacts) to decide if a full replacement is warranted.
